cards.text: Many years later, Artaxerxes is king of Persia, and we meet a man named Ezra. His family line runs son after son, all the way back to Aaron the chief priest. Friend, I showed up with a 25-cent price sticker, and this man shows up with a FAMILY FOREST.

cards.question: Ezra comes up from Babylon. He's a scribe, skilled in the Law of ___.
Ezra makes requests of the king of Persia, and the king grants ALL of them. What reason does the text give?

answers.text: The hand of the LORD was upon him
He served as the king's cupbearer
He had once saved the king's life

cards.text: Cut to the seventh year of King Artaxerxes. Ezra's bags are packed, and he's headed up to Jerusalem.

cards.question: Ezra makes the trip up to Jerusalem all by himself.

cards.text: Ezra leaves Babylon on the first day of the first month. He arrives in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month.

cards.question: So Ezra's trip from Babylon to Jerusalem takes ___ months.

cards.text: FOUR MONTHS on the road, and I get antsy waiting on a ten-minute oven timer! He made it, because "the gracious hand of his God was upon him."

cards.question: Ezra set his heart to study the Law of the LORD, then leave living it out to everybody else.
Ezra set his heart to study the Law of the LORD and to practice it. What's the third thing he set his heart to do?

cards.text: Now we get the actual letter King Artaxerxes gave Ezra, and he opens by calling himself "king of kings." Friend, my whole title is a name somebody carved into my handle.

cards.question: In the king's letter, only the priests and Levites are allowed to go up to Jerusalem with Ezra.

cards.text: The king AND his seven counselors are sending Ezra off with a job to do. Seven counselors! The only second opinion I get around here is from the oven.

cards.question: Ezra is sent to evaluate Judah and Jerusalem according to the ___ of his God, which is in his hand.

cards.text: Then comes the money. Ezra carries silver and gold the king and his counselors FREELY offered to the God of Israel, plus silver and gold from the province of Babylon and freewill offerings from the people and priests.

cards.question: With all that silver and gold, what does the king tell Ezra to buy?

answers.text: Animals to offer on the altar
Stone and timber for the walls

cards.question: Whatever silver and gold is left over, Ezra has to send back to the king.

cards.text: Ezra must deliver to the God of Jerusalem all the articles given for the service of His house. And if God's house needs anything else, the king says to pay for it from the royal treasury.
Then King Artaxerxes writes to all his treasurers west of the Euphrates about whatever Ezra the priest may require of them. I bet those treasurers got REAL quiet reading this one.

cards.question: Whatever Ezra requires, how quickly must the treasurers west of the Euphrates provide it?

cards.text: There are limits, though: up to a hundred talents of silver, a hundred cors of wheat, a hundred baths of wine and a hundred baths of olive oil.

cards.question: Silver, wheat, wine and olive oil each have a limit. But the treasurers must provide ___ without limit.
King Artaxerxes says whatever the God of heaven commands must be done diligently for His house. What reason does the king give?

answers.text: So wrath won't fall on his realm and sons
So the people will keep paying their taxes
So his own name is honored in Jerusalem

cards.question: The treasurers can still charge tribute and tolls to the priests, Levites and other servants of God's house.

cards.text: Then the king turns to Ezra himself, a man who has the wisdom of his God.

cards.question: Ezra is to appoint ___ and ___ for all the people west of the Euphrates who know the laws of his God.

cards.text: Ezra is also to teach these laws to anyone who doesn't know them. And whoever won't keep the law of Ezra's God and the law of the king faces strict judgment.

cards.question: The king's letter is done, and now Ezra speaks for himself. Who does Ezra bless for putting it into the king's heart to honor God's house in Jerusalem?

answers.text: The LORD the God of his fathers
The governor west of the Euphrates

cards.text: Ezra says the LORD has shown him favor before the king, his counselors and all the king's powerful officials. And because the hand of the LORD his God was upon him, Ezra took courage and gathered the leaders of Israel to return with him.
Look at him, friend: the letter, the silver, the gold AND the leaders. Pause right there, because this story is NOT done.
